item.title: Iran claims another attack targeting U.S. radar site in Bahrain
item.description: Iran has claimed to hit U.S. radar systems in Bahrain three times in less than a week, but authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted.

item.title: Jensen Huang says he's willing to return as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang said in a new statement that he's willing to return as Nvidia CEO if asked by the board after he resigned last week following his affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Huang also agreed to testify before Congress about his affair. Jacob Sonenshine, a markets reporter at Barron's, joins with more.

item.title: Mamdani disbands NYPD unit accused of excessive force, keeping campaign promise
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has announced the disbandment of the NYPD's Strategic Response Unit, which has been accused of using excessive force against protesters. CBS News' Anna Schecter has more.

item.title: Nvidia forms export control panel amid concerns over China sales
item.description: Chipmaker creates new committee amid growing concerns that it has allowed restricted products to reach China.

item.title: Anthropic files for IPO as it competes for AI dominance
item.description: Anthropic, which developed the Claude chatbot, is barreling ahead with its public offering despite mounting concerns about AI going rogue.

item.title: NSA's classified internal network goes down, sources say
item.description: Two U.S. officials tell CBS News that so far there is no evidence of a cyberattack.

item.title: Classified NSA network goes down, sources say
item.description: The National Security Agency's internal network for sharing and storing classified information went offline Tuesday, according to multiple U.s. officials familiar with the situation. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: Ukraine and Russia trade strikes ahead of Trump's summit with Putin, Xi
item.description: Ukraine targeted a bridge linking Russia to Crimea, a region Russia annexed in 2014. CBS News' Aidan Stretch has more.

item.title: U.S. identifies remains of 6 soldiers killed in Korean War, including teens
item.description: The identifications are part of an ongoing effort to locate and identify the remains of U.S. soldiers killed in the Korean War.

item.title: U.S. officially loses measles elimination status: "What a tragedy"
item.description: The United States has lost its official measles elimination status for the first time in 26 years. Here's what to know.

item.title: Ukraine says underground gas pipeline used to mount sneak attack
item.description: Ukraine says troops spent weeks crawling through an old underground gas pipeline to get behind enemy lines and launch a surprise attack.

item.title: Groups raise concerns over DOJ's new Civil Rights Division chief
item.description: Eighteen civil rights organizations asked President Trump to withdraw his appointment of Craig Trainor as the new acting head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division.

item.title: Jensen Huang says he "would be honored" to return as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Huang addressed a petition, signed by 190,000 people, including thousands of Nvidia employees, calling for his reinstatement.

item.title: Trump reacts to Iran's "dirty bomb" threat: "We take it very seriously"
item.description: President Trump says the U.S. is taking a potential Iranian threat against Washington, D.C., "very seriously." This comes ahead of his planned summit with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: U.S. backslides on measles elimination progress
item.description: Measles cases have more than doubled in the U.S. since 2025. Infectious disease researcher Dr. William Schaffner shares his thoughts.

item.title: Trump in Asia for Putin, Xi summit; possible Kim meeting
item.description: The president arrived in Manila for the start of a multi-day swing in Asia, where he's scheduled to meet with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping in a highly anticipated summit.

item.title: Pope Leo calls for "less controversy, less war, less division"
item.description: The Catholic Church's first U.S.-born leader, returning from a major Latin America tour, spoke about American unity, his health, and the prospect of married priests.

item.title: Scientist fired after 6-year-old girl dies in gene-editing trial
item.description: The girl died last year after receiving experimental gene therapy to correct a non-life-threatening condition, an investigation found.

item.title: Hawley, Durbin introduce Roblox safety bill ahead of hearing
item.description: The legislation would allow families of individuals harmed by tech products to take their claims to court even if they agreed to the company's terms of service for private arbitration.

item.title: Parents, gamers ask lawmakers to pass Roblox safety legislation
item.description: Some parents claim online predators have been able to groom and abuse children through the gaming platform Roblox. Lawmakers will hear from users who say they experienced abuse in a hearing. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent reports.

item.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO agrees to testify to Congress amid affair probe
item.description: The former Nvidia chief will appear for closed-door testimony on Dec. 1 after Republicans threatened to subpoena him.

item.title: Congress fights over air traffic control funds; midair collision families push for safety measures
item.description: Lawmakers are meeting over last week's nationwide FAA ground stop and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's push for more funding. Plus, the families of victims in the 2025 midair collision over the Potomac River are calling for enhanced safety measures. CBS News' Caitlin Huey-Burns has the latest.

item.title: Airlines race to recover from tech troubles before holiday season
item.description: A slate of tech problems impacted U.S. tech companies and banks and delayed flights just days after a national ground stop. CBS News' Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: Christina Ricci on the final season of "Yellowjackets"
item.description: Christina Ricci joins "CBS Mornings" to talk about the fourth and final season of the hit series "Yellowjackets," which premieres Nov. 20 on Paramount+.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that could help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Widespread service outages at major U.S. banks appear to be over
item.description: Customers at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and other major financial institutions reported difficulty accessing their accounts.

item.title: Biden lashes out at Trump in new memoir
item.description: Presidential historian Doug Brinkley joins CBS News with more on former President Biden's new memoir, "Promise Me, America."

item.title: Protests flare in Philippines over Trump's visit and planned AI hub
item.description: Protests against President Trump's visit to the Philippines have popped up around the country, as local residents criticize a Trump administration project to build an artificial intelligence hub.

item.title: Epstein's death may not have been suicide, new analysis suggests
item.description: Forensics expert Dr. Michael Freeman says multiple images and overlooked details about Jeffrey Epstein's death contradict the conclusion that he died by suicide.

item.title: Biden library nears site decision as fundraising lags
item.description: After a quiet 2025, Biden's presidential library foundation landed two $5 million gifts, but some allies are said to be frustrated donors haven't come calling.
